checks.title: The DrataAutopilotRole role (if it exists) has the SecurityAudit managed policy

verify.pass_when_text: If the account does not have the DrataAutopilotRole role, the check is N/A (empty), never PASS: there is nothing to verify. The account's other roles are not evaluated. If it exists, it has the AWS-managed policy arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/SecurityAudit attached (a policy of your own named SecurityAudit does not count). Without it Drata cannot read the infrastructure and test 123 (Cloud Infrastructure Linked to Drata) fails. The check does not verify the role's trust relationship or external ID: Drata validates that when connecting.

steps: Attach the SecurityAudit managed policy to the DrataAutopilotRole role.
Verify that the role has it and wait for the next Drata cycle (or retry test 123 from Drata).
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name DrataAutopilotRole --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/SecurityAudit
remediation.notes: No downtime. It is a read-only policy. attach-role-policy is idempotent. Drata also requires Drata's trusted account and a tenant-specific external ID in the role's trust relationship: they are not changed by this command.

checks.title: The DrataAutopilotRole role (if it exists) allows backup:ListRecoveryPointsByResource and backup:ListBackupJobs

verify.pass_when_text: If the account does not have the DrataAutopilotRole role, the check is N/A (empty), never PASS: there is nothing to verify. The account's other roles are not evaluated. If it exists, an inline or customer-managed policy of the role allows both actions (with Resource "*"; wildcard forms such as backup:List* are accepted) and no policy of that kind denies them. AWS-managed policies are not read: if the role has any, detail.aws_managed_not_evaluated names it. Without those permissions Drata tests 132 (Daily backup job status monitored) and 133 (Failed Backup Alerts Being Sent) fail. A Condition on the Allow, NotAction or a Resource other than "*" are not modeled: they do not count as a granted permission.

steps: Add to the DrataAutopilotRole role an inline policy with the AWS Backup permissions that Drata requires.
Verify the policy and wait for the next Drata cycle.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name DrataAutopilotRole --policy-name DrataBackupMonitoring --policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["backup:ListRecoveryPointsByResource","backup:ListBackupJobs"],"Resource":"*"}]}'
remediation.notes: No downtime. Read-only access to AWS Backup metadata. put-role-policy with a name that already exists replaces that policy: if the role already has an inline policy of its own, choose another name. Drata documents this inline policy as the extra requirement of tests 132, 133, 134 and 301.

checks.title: The vanta-auditor role (if it exists) has SecurityAudit and the VantaAdditionalPermissions managed policy (not inline)

verify.pass_when_text: If the account does not have the vanta-auditor role, the check is N/A (empty), never PASS: there is nothing to verify. The account's other roles are not evaluated. If it exists, it has the AWS-managed policy SecurityAudit attached and a customer-managed policy (of this account) named VantaAdditionalPermissions. An inline policy with that name is not detected by Vanta: it fails, and detail.additional_permissions says inline, absent or customer-managed. The check does not verify the content of VantaAdditionalPermissions or the trust relationship.

steps: If SecurityAudit is missing, attach it to the vanta-auditor role.

Create the customer-managed policy VantaAdditionalPermissions with the current content from the Vanta console (the base is a Deny on datapipeline and rds:DownloadDBLogFilePortion; Vanta's optional products add permissions).
Attach VantaAdditionalPermissions to the vanta-auditor role.
Only if the check reported an inline policy with that name and the previous step already attached it, delete the inline policy so as not to leave a duplicate.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name vanta-auditor --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/SecurityAudit

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws iam create-policy --policy-name VantaAdditionalPermissions --policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Deny","Action":["datapipeline:EvaluateExpression","datapipeline:QueryObjects","rds:DownloadDBLogFilePortion"],"Resource":"*"}]}'

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name vanta-auditor --policy-arn "arn:aws:iam::$ACCOUNT_ID:policy/VantaAdditionalPermissions"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name vanta-auditor --policy-arn "arn:aws:iam::$ACCOUNT_ID:policy/VantaAdditionalPermissions" && aws iam delete-role-policy --role-name vanta-auditor --policy-name VantaAdditionalPermissions
remediation.notes: No downtime. The blocks are independent: run only those that match the finding's detail (SecurityAudit is missing; the policy does not exist yet; attach it; delete the inline one). The last block deletes the inline policy only if the attach succeeded (it is chained with &&); do not run it if the role does not have an inline policy with that name. The VantaAdditionalPermissions content shown is only the base: copy the current one from the Vanta console (Connect AWS) to include the permissions of the products in use (CodeCommit, IAM Identity Center...). create-policy fails if the policy already exists.

checks.title: The key policies of own KMS keys allow the auditor roles (Drata and Vanta) the read actions

verify.pass_when_text: For each customer-managed KMS key (not pending deletion) and each auditor role that exists in the account (DrataAutopilotRole, vanta-auditor), the key policy allows the role the read actions: kms:DescribeKey and kms:GetKeyRotationStatus for Drata (test 223), and kms:DescribeKey, GetPublicKey, ListAliases, ListGrants, ListKeyPolicies, ListResourceTags and ListRetirableGrants for Vanta. A statement that names the role, or the delegation to the account root (Principal arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:root with kms:*, the "Enable IAM User Permissions" statement), which hands the decision to the role's IAM policies, is valid. kms:ListKeys is not required in the key policy: it is not an action on a key. An Allow with a Condition is not modeled and does not count; a Deny on the role and the action does count against, and a Deny with NotPrincipal applies to every principal that is not listed: it affects the role unless the role (or the root of its account) is in NotPrincipal. If neither of the two roles exists, or the key is an AWS-managed one, the result is N/A (empty), never PASS. If the key policy prevents the auditor from reading the key (AccessDenied), that key ends up NOT_VERIFIED with the missing permission and the others are evaluated.

vault_signals: acceso de auditoría a las claves

steps: Read the current key policy of {resource_id} and save it to a file.

Add a statement that allows the auditor roles that exist the read actions, without removing the current statements (if the Drata or the Vanta role does not exist, remove its ARN from the Principal: KMS rejects principals that do not exist).
Review the new file and apply it with put-key-policy, which replaces the entire policy.
Verify the policy and wait for the next Drata and Vanta cycle.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
KEY_ID="{resource_id}"
KEY_FILE="${KEY_ID##*/}"
# read-only: fetches the current key policy into a file; the name carries the key id so as not to apply another key's by mistake
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id "$KEY_ID" --policy-name default --region "$REGION" --query Policy --output text > "key-policy-$KEY_FILE.json"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
KEY_ID="{resource_id}"
KEY_FILE="${KEY_ID##*/}"
STATEMENT='{"Sid":"AllowAuditorRead","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":["arn:aws:iam::'"$ACCOUNT_ID"':role/DrataAutopilotRole","arn:aws:iam::'"$ACCOUNT_ID"':role/vanta-auditor"]},"Action":["kms:DescribeKey","kms:GetKeyRotationStatus","kms:GetPublicKey","kms:ListAliases","kms:ListGrants","kms:ListKeyPolicies","kms:ListResourceTags","kms:ListRetirableGrants"],"Resource":"*"}'
# applies nothing: adds the statement to the policy that was read (keeps all the others) and shows the result for review
rm -f "key-policy-$KEY_FILE-new.json"
if [ ! -s "key-policy-$KEY_FILE.json" ]; then echo "STOPPED: key-policy-$KEY_FILE.json is missing (or empty); run the first block first"; else jq --argjson statement "$STATEMENT" '.Statement += [$statement]' "key-policy-$KEY_FILE.json" > "key-policy-$KEY_FILE-new.json" && cat "key-policy-$KEY_FILE-new.json"; fi

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
KEY_ID="{resource_id}"
KEY_FILE="${KEY_ID##*/}"
# put-key-policy REPLACES the whole policy: apply only the reviewed file (key-policy-$KEY_FILE-new.json)
if [ -s "key-policy-$KEY_FILE-new.json" ]; then aws kms put-key-policy --key-id "$KEY_ID" --policy-name default --policy "file://key-policy-$KEY_FILE-new.json" --region "$REGION"; else echo "STOPPED: key-policy-$KEY_FILE-new.json is missing; run the previous blocks first"; fi
remediation.verify_after: aws kms get-key-policy --key-id "{resource_id}" --policy-name default --region "{region}" --query Policy --output text
remediation.notes: No downtime, but high risk: put-key-policy replaces the entire policy and a wrong policy can leave the key without administrators. Always keep the current statements, especially the one that delegates to the account root, and review key-policy-new.json before the third block; do not run it if the second block failed (in that case it shows STOPPED and the third applies nothing). The temporary files carry the key id (key-policy-<id>.json and key-policy-<id>-new.json) so as not to apply another key's by mistake when there are several. Keys from another account are fixed from the owning account. The statement grants each role the union of the Drata and Vanta actions: split it into one statement per role if you want least privilege. If the key policy already delegates to the account root with kms:*, the check passes without changes (the auditor roles get in through their IAM policies, which include SecurityAudit).
